correctness.rationale: For each edge uv, a forbidden pair of selected edges separated by that third edge is exactly the condition (d_B(u)-epsilon_uv)(d_B(v)-epsilon_uv)>0. The five parent-edge/selected-child-count boundary states partition all choices, and each recurrence follows from the local condition; induction over rooted subtrees proves exactness including leaf, singleton-tree and root boundaries. Incremental polynomial products cost O(n²) coefficient-arithmetic operations by charging pairs to their unique lowest common ancestor. Independent brute-force conflict checks, not relying on the local lemma, matched all 1,119,263 subsets across 18,249 labeled trees through seven vertices; further 860 larger generated trees passed sanity checks. The finite tests are not a proof of all cases.

value.rationale: Edge-open packing is a motivated graph invariant with previously published tree maximum algorithms. Knowing only the scalar optimum leaves all feasible cardinality counts and the number of optimal configurations undetermined; the five-state recurrence computes this entire natural invariant for every finite tree with an explicit O(n²) arithmetic bound and yields the complete maximum-set multiplicity. It is a structural counting theorem rather than a single tiny instance or mechanical restatement of an existing formula. The computation is reproducible and the output has concrete uses in the distribution of injective edge-coloring classes. The result does not claim an asymptotically optimal algorithm or a complexity separation.
